item.title: Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT)
item.description: Overview Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a medical procedure that runs electrical currents to the brain and triggers seizures for mental health conditions that are otherwise treatment-resistant.

item.title: Ego
item.description: Overview In philosophical and psychological contexts, “ego” doesn’t have the connotation of a negative byproduct of arrogance or narcissism; instead, it refers to an aspect of our identity that we construct as the “I.” Unconscious or subconscious feelings are generally considered outside of the ego’...

item.title: MDMA
item.description: Overview 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, also known as MDMA, ecstacy, and molly, is a psychedelic stimulant known to cause euphoria, heightened senses, and deep emotional connections.

item.title: Eating Disorder (ED)
item.description: Overview Eating disorders are patterns of consumption that are based in an unhealthy level of concern about caloric intake, weight gain, body image, or relationship to food.

item.title: Early Maladaptive Schema (EMS)
item.description: Overview Under the Schema Therapy model advanced by Jeffrey Young, an early maladaptive schema (EMS) is a recurring pattern or core belief that develops in childhood or adolescence that serves as a source of dysfunction throughout one’s life.

item.title: Dysmorphia
item.description: Overview Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), often called dysmorphia as a shorthand, is a mental health condition in which someone is obsessively preoccupied with an apparent flaw that might be minor or nonexistent.

item.title: Drug Consumption Room (DCR)
item.description: Overview Drug Consumption Rooms (DCRs), also referred to as a supervised injection site or overdose prevention center (OPC), are facilities where someone can use substances they’ve obtained while under medical supervision as part of harm reduction policies.
